predict.question: If you stretch a rubber band tight and pluck it, then loosen it and pluck again, what will change?

options.text: The loose band will make a lower, slower sound while the tight one sounds higher
The loose band will sound louder and higher at the same time
Nothing will change, both sound the same

predict.why: A tighter band vibrates faster, giving more vibrations per second and a higher pitch, while looseness slows the vibration.

experiment.title: Rubber Band Twang Test
steps: Stretch a rubber band around an empty plastic bottle lengthwise
Pluck it gently and watch and listen
Now stretch it tighter by pulling more and pluck again
Compare the sound and how fast the band moves
Try pressing a ruler lightly near the band while it vibrates to feel it shake
experiment.note: Pluck gently, don't snap the band hard on fingers.

say: Did the band move fast or slow each time?
Was the tight one higher or lower in sound?
Can you feel it shaking if you touch it lightly?
avoid: Don't say 'tight means high pitch' before they notice it themselves

notice.question: What did you see and hear when the band was loose versus tight?
notice.lookFor: Child notices the band moves (vibrates) and that tighter/faster vibration gives higher-pitched sound

hints.text: Watch the band itself, not just listen
Compare how fast it shakes when loose versus tight
Faster shaking makes a different kind of sound than slower shaking

reveal.explanation: Sound is made when something vibrates back and forth quickly. When the rubber band vibrates fast, it makes a high-pitched sound; when it vibrates slowly, the pitch is low. Loudness is different—it depends on how big the vibration is, not how fast. Sound also needs something like air to travel through; it cannot travel through empty space.
reveal.termMeaning: Frequency is how many vibrations happen per second (controls pitch), amplitude is how big each vibration is (controls loudness).

teachBack.prompt: Explain to a younger sibling why a tight rubber band sounds different from a loose one, using the word 'vibrate'.

revisits.question: Why does a thin guitar string usually sound higher than a thick one?
revisits.answer: Thin strings vibrate faster, giving higher frequency and higher pitch

revisits.question: Can astronauts in space hear sound directly through empty space?
revisits.answer: No, sound needs a medium like air; space is empty so sound cannot travel
